text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Negotiations between Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and opposition parties to form a three-party coalition government stretched out until late Sunday night. Ouyahia has set the pass mark at four ministries and two secretary of state positions for each of the two would-be junior partners, the Islamist-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) and National Liberation Front (FLN). The main party in the coalition will be the National Democratic Rally.
- Ouyahia holds talks with MPS leader Mahfoud Nahnah and FLN chief Boualem Benhmaouda on government formation proposals. The two party leaders are holding their replies until Monday.
- The MPS and FLN have accepted offers by Ouyahia who is seeking a wide consensus in the government line-up which will be in charge of preparing and supervising the next local elections.

- Algeria and Mauritania attend Lisbon direct talks between Polisario Front and Morocco on the Western Sahara conflict. The talks will be a moment of hope and also a moment of truth where the two sides are to underline their positions in the presence of U.N. envoy James Baker.
